radiology_report:
Tergooi MC
Department of Radiology
Date: 12 December 2024
Exam: Multiparametric MRI prostate
Clinical indication: PSA 7.9 ng/mL, prior biopsy Gleason 4+3. Evaluate for focal lesion and local staging.
FINDINGS: The prostate volume measures 123.0 mL. T2-weighted imaging shows a focal area of low signal intensity in the left peripheral zone at the apex. This region demonstrates restricted diffusion on DWI with corresponding high signal on the ADC map and early enhancement on DCE sequences, consistent with a PI-RADS 4 lesion. The lesion measures approximately 14 mm in its greatest dimension. No extracapsular extension or seminal vesicle invasion is identified. No suspicious lymphadenopathy or bone lesions are seen.
IMPRESSION: PI-RADS 4 lesion in the left peripheral zone apex. Prostate volume 123.0 mL, PSA density 0.07 ng/mL/mL. Clinical stage cT1c. csPCa predicted probability 0.76090467.

previous_notes.author: Dr. R. van den Berg (GP)
previous_notes.text: 13 May 2024 - Dr. R. van den Berg (GP): Patient presented for routine follow-up with a PSA of 4.3 ng/mL, representing a significant rise from previous measurements. Given the upward trend and prior biopsy history, a referral to urology was initiated for further evaluation and potential re-biopsy planning. The patient was advised to continue current comorbidity management.

pathology_report:
Biopsy timepoint 1: Histological examination of the prostate tissue reveals a Gleason score of 4+3, corresponding to ISUP grade group 3. The architecture is characterized by fusion and a single large cribriform field. A cribriform pattern is present. The tumour is located in the peripheral zone, apex left.

Summary: The histological findings remain consistent across the available biopsy timepoint, demonstrating ISUP grade group 3 disease with high-risk architectural features in the left peripheral zone.

AI-predicted ISUP grade group (digital pathology): grade group 5.
